heading: How Our BMI Calculator Works (Step by Step)
alt: A BMI calculator takes height and weight, divides weight by height squared, then matches the result to a CDC category

heading: 3. How we interpret your BMI result (adults 20+)
alt: Adult BMI categories: underweight under 18.5, healthy 18.5 to 25, overweight 25 to 30, obesity classes from 30 up

heading: 4. Adults vs. children and teens
alt: Adult BMI uses fixed cut-offs; for ages 2 to 19 it is read as percentiles for age and sex on a separate calculator

heading: The Limits of BMI (Why It’s Not the Whole Story)
alt: BMI misleads for muscular people, older adults with less muscle, different ethnic thresholds, and where fat is stored

heading: Other measures your provider may use
alt: Beyond BMI a provider checks waist circumference, blood pressure and labs, fitness level, and eating, sleep and mood

heading: How to Use Our BMI Calculator in a Healthy, Helpful Way
alt: Use a BMI result well: enter honest numbers, notice the category and your reaction, ask a professional, recheck at visits

heading: What Healthy Weight Loss Actually Means
alt: Healthy weight loss runs 0.5 to 2 pounds a week, counts non-scale wins, and treats BMI as a screening tool only

heading: Evidence-Based Nutrition Patterns That Work
alt: Sustainable weight loss nutrition: 20 to 40g protein per meal, 25 to 38g fiber daily, healthy fats, and water first

heading: Movement: Training for Fat Loss and Lifelong Health
alt: Weight loss movement: 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly, strength on two days, and hourly movement breaks

heading: Sleep, Stress, and the Metabolism Connection
alt: Sleep 7 to 9 hours, take short stress breaks, and keep protein and fiber snacks ready for your known trigger times

heading: Medical Weight Management: When Clinical Support Helps
alt: Clinical weight loss support: eligibility review, coaching, FDA-approved medication, and surgery for qualified patients

heading: Special Considerations
alt: Weight loss considerations for PCOS and menopause, diabetes, hypertension and lipids, and older adults

heading: Safety First: When to Seek Care
alt: Stop and call a clinician during weight loss for dizziness or fainting, chest pain or palpitations, or rapid unexplained loss

heading: A 4-Week, Real-Life Kickstart
alt: A four-week weight loss kickstart: foundations, then fiber and planning, then skills and social life, then review
